subject: test-planner
reason: Basket.API service rules and NOT_FOUND/UNAUTHENTICATED paths at the unit layer, Redis persistence and delete/legacy-load at the functional layer, and the cart-page flows for AC1, 2, 3, 5, 7 and 10 at e2e; this update adds TC-CART-1-23, kept for PR-check finding ACC-SEED-1 (a saved product missing from the catalog is skipped).

excluded.item: Limit on saved products, anonymous saved products, price changes of saved products
excluded.reason: out of scope per Test scope

excluded.item: AC4 and AC8 in the browser
excluded.reason: Test scope places them at the API layer; covered by TC-CART-1-03 and TC-CART-1-06

excluded.item: SaveForLater of a product already saved
excluded.reason: undefined by the story (see Open questions)

excluded.item: Move to cart / Remove offered for a saved product missing from the catalog
excluded.reason: undefined by the story (see Open questions); TC-CART-1-23 asserts only the fixed skip behaviour

excluded.item: Whether the basket key is deleted when nothing is saved
excluded.reason: undefined by the story (see Open questions); TC-CART-1-12 asserts the observable empty basket
undefined by the story (see Open questions)

excluded.item: Order line contents on the orders page
excluded.reason: UI shows no order lines; TC-CART-1-20 checks the order total (see Open questions)

excluded.item: Whether the header badge counts quantities
excluded.reason: not stated by the story (see Open questions)

items.title: SaveForLater moves the whole cart line, with its quantity, to saved items
covers: AC1
Save for later button: moves the whole line, with its quantity
items.reason: AC1 core API behavior: the line must leave the cart and arrive in saved with the same quantity, and the other line must stay. A unit test with a mocked repository checks this cheaply; the UI view of it is TC-CART-1-16.

items.title: MoveToCart puts the saved product, with its quantity, into an empty cart
covers: AC3
Move to cart button: moves the saved product, with its quantity, back to the cart
items.reason: AC3: the quantity must survive the move and the saved list must be left without the product. Unit layer, mocked repository.

items.title: MoveToCart adds the saved quantity to a product already in the cart
covers: AC4
Move to cart: if the cart already has that product, the quantities are added together
items.reason: AC4: merging, not replacing or duplicating the line. Separate from TC-CART-1-02 because it exercises the merge branch.

items.title: RemoveSavedItem deletes the saved product and leaves the cart unchanged
covers: AC5
Remove button: deletes the saved product, the cart is unchanged
items.reason: AC5: Remove must not touch cart lines or other saved products. Unit layer, mocked repository.

items.title: GetBasket returns saved products next to the cart items
covers: Outputs: getting the basket returns the saved products (product id and quantity) next to the cart items
items.reason: The WebApp reads saved products from this response; if they were missing the section could never render after a reload. Unit layer, mocked repository.

items.title: UpdateBasket never changes saved products
covers: AC8
Updating the cart items never adds, changes or removes saved products
items.reason: AC8: the WebApp's add-to-cart goes through UpdateBasket, which carries no saved items; if the service overwrote the stored basket, adding a product would silently drop everything saved.

items.title: SaveForLater of a product that is not in the cart fails with NOT_FOUND
covers: AC9
Saving a product that is not in the cart fails with NOT_FOUND and changes nothing
items.reason: AC9: the story names NOT_FOUND and "changes nothing"; the risk is a phantom saved item or a partial write. Unit layer asserts the repository is never written.

items.title: MoveToCart of a product that is not saved fails with NOT_FOUND
covers: AC9
Moving a product that is not saved fails with NOT_FOUND and changes nothing
items.reason: AC9, move branch. Separate from TC-CART-1-07 because it is a different operation with its own lookup; the product is in the cart, so a wrong implementation that looks at the cart would succeed.

items.title: RemoveSavedItem of a product that is not saved fails with NOT_FOUND
covers: AC9
Removing a product that is not saved fails with NOT_FOUND and changes nothing
items.reason: AC9, remove branch; the product is in the cart and must not be removed from it by mistake.

items.title: SaveForLater, MoveToCart and RemoveSavedItem reject an anonymous caller
covers: Outputs: every operation still requires a signed-in user (UNAUTHENTICATED otherwise)
items.reason: The story requires the new operations to keep the auth rule; one case with the three calls because they share the behavior and the same assertion, mirroring the existing `UpdateBasketRejectsAnonymousUser`.

items.title: DeleteBasketAsync empties the cart and keeps the saved products in Redis
covers: AC7
Deleting the basket empties the cart and keeps the saved products
items.reason: AC7 depends on the order-started handler calling DeleteBasket; if it removed the Redis key, the saved list would be lost at checkout. Needs real Redis serialization, hence functional.

items.title: DeleteBasketAsync with nothing saved leaves an empty cart and nothing saved
covers: Outputs: Deleting the basket empties the cart (nothing saved)
items.reason: Guards the other branch of the delete: a basket without saved products must behave as before this story (the existing round-trip test does not assert saved products at all).

items.title: Saved products round-trip through Redis and are still there when read by a new repository instance
covers: AC6
Saved products live with the basket in Redis
items.reason: AC6 (sign out and in) is storage persistence, not session state. The service tests mock the repository, so only a real Redis case proves the `SavedItems` JSON property is written and read with product id and quantity intact; a second repository instance on the same connection proves it is stored, not cached in memory. This one case replaces the former separate round-trip case (a plain repository round-trip says nothing about AC1 or AC8, so it claims only AC6).

items.title: A basket stored without a SavedItems property loads with an empty saved list
covers: Technical Notes: a basket stored before this change has no saved products and must still load
items.reason: Existing customers' baskets in Redis predate this change; a null or failed deserialization would break their cart page after deploy.

items.title: Pressing Save for later on a cart line moves it to the Saved for later section
covers: AC1
Outputs: Saved for later (N) section, Save for later button, total and badge
items.reason: AC1 end to end: button wiring, section heading with N, saved line contents, and that total and badge exclude saved products. Needs the real browser and stack.

items.title: An empty cart with saved products shows the empty message and the Saved for later section
covers: AC2
Outputs: empty cart with saved products shows the empty-cart message and the section below it
items.reason: AC2: the page has an early branch for an empty cart; the risk is that the saved section is hidden there and the shopper believes the saved products are lost.

items.title: Move to cart returns the saved product to the cart and hides the section
covers: Move to cart button: moves the saved product, with its quantity, back to the cart (cart has other products)
Outputs: section not shown when nothing is saved
items.reason: The `Move to cart` input rule in the browser when the cart already has other products (no merge): the saved quantity is kept, the existing lines are untouched, and the section disappears once the last saved product moves. AC3's literal empty-cart precondition is TC-CART-1-22.

items.title: Remove deletes the saved product and leaves the cart unchanged
covers: AC5
Remove button: deletes the saved product, the cart is unchanged
items.reason: AC5 in the browser: the button deletes rather than moves, and the cart total and badge stay put.

items.title: Placing an order orders only the cart items and keeps the saved product
covers: AC7
Saved products are not part of the order placed at checkout
items.reason: AC7 is the cross-service risk: checkout deletes the basket, which must not lose saved products, and the order must not include them.

items.title: Bob does not see alice's saved products
covers: AC10
Saved products belong to one shopper
items.reason: AC10: isolation between shoppers; the basket is keyed by user id and a shared key would leak saved products.

items.title: Move to cart from an empty cart puts the saved product with its quantity in the cart
covers: AC3
AC2
items.reason: AC3 exactly as stated (cart empty, product saved with quantity 2): the saved quantity is kept and the Saved for later section is no longer shown. A separate scenario seeds the empty cart directly, so AC2's starting state is also read from storage on the first page load rather than built through the UI as in TC-CART-1-17.

items.title: The cart page renders and skips a saved product that is no longer in the catalog
covers: PR check ACC-SEED-1: saved product no longer in the catalog
Outputs: Saved for later (N) section
Outputs: saved products not in the order total
items.reason: Regression case for PR check finding ACC-SEED-1, which the PR check upheld and fixed (0b70c06): a saved product whose catalog item was removed broke the cart page. The story's PR-check notes record the fixed behaviour (the page renders and skips that product), so the code after the fix is the contract here. It needs e2e because the failure is in how `CartPage.razor` joins saved products with catalog data, which only the running WebApp against the real Catalog API exercises.

subject: test-planner
reason: Every acceptance criterion, Output rule, auth rule and the legacy-basket load are covered with concrete expectations at the layers the Test scope names; only TC-CART-1-22's wording about when the Saved for later heading is absent is self-contradictory as written.

items.reason: Expected result says no 'Saved for later' heading exists 'before and after the reload', which literally contradicts the first bullet expecting 'Saved for later (1)' before the move. Restate as: absent after step 2 (the move) and after step 3 (the reload).

subject: test-automation
reason: All 23 cases are implemented faithfully: unit tests assert exact response lines and repository writes or non-writes, Redis functional tests use real serialization, and the e2e specs sign in as seeded users, assert exact totals, badges, headings, lines and absences with web-first waits; every UI keyframe I opened matches its case. One point off for the sign-in and locator helpers copied unchanged across three spec files (lesson L1).

items.reason: signIn() and the locator helpers (cartLines, cartLine, savedSection, savedLine, savedHeading, orderTotal, badge) are copied unchanged into cart-1.spec.ts, cart-1-saved.spec.ts and cart-1-missing.spec.ts; they belong in one shared module under e2e/teststack/ (lesson L1: duplicated helpers). Also affects TC-CART-1-16..22.
